title: The Expanding Universe
hook: Distant galaxies are rushing away from us, and the farther one is, the faster it flees — not because they're moving through space, but because space itself is stretching.
key_points: Hubble found distant galaxies are receding, faster the farther away they are.
Space itself is stretching, carrying galaxies apart from one another.
Their light is stretched to longer, redder wavelengths — called redshift.
Running the expansion backward points to the Big Bang.
content_html: In the 1920s Edwin Hubble noticed something startling: nearly every distant galaxy is moving away from us, and the more distant it is, the faster it goes. The natural reading isn't that we sit at the center of a cosmic stampede. Instead, space itself is expanding, and that expansion carries the galaxies apart from one another.
extra_html: We measure this through redshift. As light from a receding galaxy crosses the stretching space between us, its waves get stretched too, shifting toward the longer, redder end of the spectrum — and the bigger the shift, the faster the recession. Play the expansion in reverse and everything converges toward a hot, dense beginning, which is exactly what the Big Bang describes. Wikipedia explains how the expansion was discovered and what redshift reveals about it.

related.title: The Big Bang
related.hook: About 13.8 billion years ago the universe began hot and dense and has been expanding ever since — but it wasn't an explosion into empty space. Space itself stretched.

related.title: Dark Matter & Dark Energy
related.hook: Everything we can see — stars, planets, people — is only about 5% of the universe. The other 95% is two mysteries we've never directly detected.

flashcards.prompt: What did Edwin Hubble discover about distant galaxies?
flashcards.back_html: They are rushing away from us, and the farther a galaxy is, the faster it recedes — a sign the universe is expanding.

choices.text: Space itself is stretching, carrying galaxies along with it
Galaxies are flying through static, unchanging space
They are being pushed by starlight

flashcards.explanation_html: Galaxies aren't speeding through space so much as being carried apart by the expansion of space itself.

choices.text: Light from receding galaxies stretched to longer, redder wavelengths
Galaxies literally glowing red from heat
A reddening caused by Earth's atmosphere

flashcards.explanation_html: As space stretches, the light traveling through it stretches too, shifting toward the red end of the spectrum.
